summary: F5 review of PR #9 found the registry-root move mechanically strong: PR checks passed and live grep evidence found no residual registries/cross-cutting references outside preserved historical evidence/ADR context. Remaining maintainability risk is semantic drift from broad text rewrites into handoff/plan artifacts and a deferred specs flattening dependency. Highest severity: MAJOR.

findings.issue: The path rewrite changed handoff instructions into a contradictory rule: it now says no new durables in `/registry` while also saying new durables go to `/registry/`. Because .omc handoffs can be reused by agents, this creates ambiguous future instructions rather than a purely mechanical path migration.
findings.remediation: Review every rewritten .omc handoff/plan sentence semantically, not just by string replacement. For historical handoffs, either preserve original text with an explicit migrated_path annotation or update the whole rule so it distinguishes retired roots from the new canonical registry root.

findings.issue: ADR-0115 says historical evidence under evidence/debate and evidence/per-change was preserved, but the PR still rewrote .omc handoffs, plans, and session-state text. That splits provenance policy by directory and makes it unclear which historical artifacts are immutable versus live control surfaces.
findings.remediation: Codify a directory-level migration policy for .omc handoffs/plans/state before additional bulk path rewrites. Add a migration verifier that distinguishes live references, historical evidence, and historical-but-consumed handoff artifacts.

findings.issue: The PR deliberately defers specs/cross-cutting flattening. That scope boundary is reasonable, but it leaves registry and specs using different topology rules during the transition.
findings.remediation: Track the specs flattening as a bounded follow-up with its own grep/assertion gate, and keep synthesis from declaring the entire cross-cutting topology flattened until that PR lands.
